before: Measured opaque widgets could extend beyond a page and repeat their complete UI on every native fallback fragment.
after: One persistent opaque widget occupies a bounded scroll viewport on its first native fallback fragment. Measurements reserve only excess viewport height. The complete native fallback remains in Word output. Each submitted widget payload action starts a separate undo unit using the existing native automation flag.
reason: Viewport limits and reservations are local view inputs. Canonical content, operations, payload formats, and collaboration protocols do not change.
